contract_plain_english: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2] Starting from the full-column-rank matrix A R_hat^{-1} supplied by Lemma 3.1, the particular finite-precision forward-substitution result Y_hat remains full column rank whenever its scaled spectral perturbation epsilon_2 is strictly below one, and its 2-norm condition number obeys the stated rational bound.

source_evidence.observation: Lemma 3.2 defines Y_hat as the finite-precision result of computing A R_hat^{-1}, sets DeltaY = Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1} and epsilon_2 = ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2, and assumes epsilon_2 < 1.
The lemma concludes both that Y_hat is full rank and that kappa_2(Y_hat) <= (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2).
The proof invokes the additive relation Y_hat = A R_hat^{-1} + DeltaY and reasoning analogous to the singular-value perturbation argument in Lemma 3.1.
The cross-referenced construction assumes epsilon_1 < 1 and then establishes that R_hat is invertible and A R_hat^{-1} is full rank.
Computing A R^{-1} by forward substitution is explained rowwise as solving R^T x_i = a_i for the rows of A R^{-1}.
The paper's standing context has A in R^{m x n}, SA in R^{s x n}, m > s > n, with both A and SA full rank.

statement.algorithm_linkage: [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909; anchor: Algorithm 1.3, step 4] This is the sketch-and-apply Blendenpik step that explicitly computes Y = A R^{-1} with forward substitution, here analyzed with the computed factors R_hat and Y_hat.
binders: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] R_hat^{-1} is the upper-triangular inverse arising from the finite-precision construction in Lemma 3.1, and Y_hat is the computed m-by-n matrix obtained from A R_hat^{-1}.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 definitions] DeltaY := Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1} and epsilon_2 := ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2.
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: standing full-rank assumption] The inherited dimensions are A in R^{m x n}, R_hat in R^{n x n}, and Y_hat and DeltaY in R^{m x n}, with m > n.
conclusions: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 first conclusion] Y_hat is full rank; under the inherited m-by-n dimensions with m > n, this means rank(Y_hat) = n, i.e. full column rank.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 displayed bound] kappa_2(Y_hat) <= (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2).
constants_and_indexing: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 hypothesis and bound] The threshold is strictly epsilon_2 < 1; the condition estimate has exactly +epsilon_2 in the numerator and 1-epsilon_2 in the denominator.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] The result has no iteration index, probabilistic constant, or index offset.
definitions_and_conventions: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 definitions] The perturbation relation is exactly Y_hat = A R_hat^{-1} + DeltaY.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: footnote 3 beneath Lemma 3.3] The dagger superscript denotes the matrix pseudoinverse.
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: definition of kappa_2(A)] The 2-norm condition number is the largest singular value divided by the smallest singular value for a full-column-rank matrix.
[PDF p. 11, printed p. 915; anchor: rowwise triangular-system computation] Forward substitution for A R_hat^{-1} means solving R_hat^T x_i = a_i row by row.
error_notions: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: definition of epsilon_2] epsilon_2 is a dimensionless spectral-norm perturbation size, scaling ||DeltaY||_2 by ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 proof] DeltaY is a forward/additive matrix-computation error, not the least-squares backward-error perturbation denoted DeltaY_hat later in Theorem 3.5.
exceptional_values: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: epsilon_2 < 1 and displayed denominator] The strict inequality makes 1-epsilon_2 positive and excludes the singular-value perturbation threshold at epsilon_2 = 1.
[PDF p. 12, printed p. 916; anchor: Lemma 3.1 invertibility conclusion] Existence of R_hat^{-1} is inherited from the conclusion that R_hat is invertible.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] Overflow, underflow, NaNs, infinities, and subnormal arithmetic are not discussed.
higher_order_terms: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 displayed bound] The rank and condition-number conclusions are exact inequalities in epsilon_2; no big-O term or omitted higher-order remainder appears.
hypotheses: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 strict hypothesis] The explicit local hypothesis is epsilon_2 < 1.

[PDF p. 12, printed p. 916; anchor: Lemma 3.1 statement] The cross-referenced construction is in the regime epsilon_1 < 1, which makes R_hat invertible and the unperturbed matrix A R_hat^{-1} full column rank.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] Y_hat is specifically obtained by forward substitution in finite precision; the result is not about an arbitrary matrix approximation.
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: standing full-rank assumption] The paper additionally assumes A and SA are full rank in its standing least-squares setting.
implicit_context: [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916; anchor: three finite-precision steps at the start of section 3] R_hat is the computed triangular factor obtained after forming the sketch SA and applying Householder QR, and Y_hat is the computed preconditioned matrix.

[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: paragraph following Lemma 3.2] The later discussion seeks to make epsilon_2 small from a condition such as kappa_2(A)u << 1, but that condition is not part of Lemma 3.2 itself.

[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: proof of Lemma 3.2] The rank conclusion inherits the full-column-rank base matrix supplied by Lemma 3.1; epsilon_2 < 1 alone would not preserve rank from a rank-deficient base.
norms: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 definitions and bound] Every displayed norm in the lemma is the spectral matrix 2-norm, and kappa_2 is the corresponding singular-value condition number.
numerical_model: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] The only local numerical model is an additive finite-precision error DeltaY in the forward-substitution computation.

[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.3 opening sentence] The surrounding analysis treats finite-precision quantities as computed with unit roundoff u, although u does not occur explicitly in Lemma 3.2.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement and proof] The lemma is deterministic conditional perturbation analysis; it contains no probability statement about the random sketch.

undebatable_constraints: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 definitions] epsilon_2 must be exactly ||Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1}||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 strict hypothesis] The preservation result requires the strict inequality epsilon_2 < 1.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 two conclusions] A faithful contract must retain both full rank of Y_hat and the displayed condition-number bound.
[PDF p. 12, printed p. 916; anchor: Lemma 3.1 statement] The unperturbed matrix A R_hat^{-1} must be full column rank; this is inherited from Lemma 3.1 rather than proved solely from epsilon_2 < 1.
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: Lemma 3.2 statement] The matrix is the finite-precision forward-substitution output, not the exact product A R_hat^{-1}.
